item.title: [LU-18826] Kernel panic due to null pointer from obd_get_mod_rpc_slot
item.description:

issue happen when to_kthread(current) == NULL . relevant source code below:

bool kthread_should_stop(void)
{
        return test_bit(KTHREAD_SHOULD_STOP, &to_kthread(current)->flags);
}


static inline struct kthread *to_kthread(struct task_struct *k)
{
        WARN_ON(!(k->flags & PF_KTHREAD));
        return (__force void *)k->set_child_tid;
}

Rootcause Analysis

  1. Kernel try to start new kthread from kthreadd by alloc_thread_stack_node
  2. Ran out of memory, try to clean up inode cache
  3. In obd_get_mod_rpc_slot, unfortunately in flight rpcs is full. So trying to put into sleep using wait_woken
  4. In kthread_should_stop -> to_kthread, it tried to read set_child_tid but it's null. It's expected since the task_struct here is kthreadd, which is still the parent one, because the allocation have not yet completed

Repro

  1. Create a dummy obd device
  2. Modify current task_struct, 
    set_child_tid: 0000000000000000, current->flags: 208840, set max_in_flight_mod_rpcs to 0 so that it will be put into sleep all the time
  3. call obd_get_mod_rpc_slot and get kernel panic
[ 1621.881498] Call trace:
[ 1621.881915]  kthread_should_stop+0x18/0x40
[ 1621.882627]  obd_get_mod_rpc_slot+0x10c/0x43c [obdclass]
[ 1621.883502]  test_obd_rpc_slot+0xdc/0x270 [task_mod]
[ 1621.884317]  task_mod_init+0x70/0x1000 [task_mod]

Proposed fix

Skip the waiting part in obd_get_mod_rpc_slot since we know it will cause kernel panic.

https://git.whamcloud.com/?p=fs/lustre-release.git;a=blob;f=lustre/obdclass/genops.c;h=93b1fe8050729d38e507a8432c67aa8dddd8987d;hb=HEAD#l2274

During the normal flow, the process will be put into sleep and be woken up by claim_mod_rpc_function.

2231         avail = cli->cl_mod_rpcs_in_flight < cli->cl_max_mod_rpcs_in_flight ||
2232                 (close_req && cli->cl_close_rpcs_in_flight == 0);
2233         if (avail) {
2234                 cli->cl_mod_rpcs_in_flight++;
2235                 if (close_req)
2236                         cli->cl_close_rpcs_in_flight++;
2237                 ret = woken_wake_function(wq_entry, mode, flags, key);
2238                 w->woken = true;
2239         } else if (cli->cl_close_rpcs_in_flight)

In this special case, the process is kthreadd, which will trigger kernel panic if put into sleep. So the modified logic will looks similar to close_req, which simply get a guaranteed slot by

2235                 if (close_req) cli->cl_close_rpcs_in_flight++;

The fix will be a similar process, except it will skip the whole enqueue process as well.

	if (! ((current->flags & PF_KTHREAD) && current->set_child_tid) ){
		// Skip wait_woken as it will cause kernel panic. Grant it a slot.
		cli->cl_mod_rpcs_in_flight++;

	} else {
// ... enqueue and wake_woken logic

shadow could you please point out where the max_mod_rpcs_in_flight limit is checked on the server? AFAICS this limit is sent to the client at connect time, and the client honors it, but I can't see an actual limit on the MDS for the number of slots a client can use.

Patch 58501 is not permanently increasing cl_mod_rpcs_in_flight, just temporarily for the request that is under PF_MEMALLOC so that it can make forward progress. Maybe the code could be cleaned up a bit to handle the cl->cl_mod_rpcs_in_flight+ and cl->cl_close_rpcs_in_flight+ in a helper function, and certainly turn the LCONSOLE_INFO(...) message into CDEBUG(D_RPCTRACE, ...) to avoid console spam.

>could you please point out where the max_mod_rpcs_in_flight limit is checked on the server?
OBD_ALLOC(exp->exp_used_slots,
BITS_TO_LONGS(OBD_MAX_RIF_MAX) * sizeof(long));
and other code related to the slots, last rcvd .. etc
so wrong slot number will cause a access outside of array.

>Patch 58501 is not permanently increasing cl_mod_rpcs_in_flight, just temporarily for the request that is under PF_MEMALLOC so that it can make forward progress.
sure. it will be increase a used slot number in such condition. in case lustre client needs to cancel a 1000 open locks under memory pleasure it will have
1000 calls cli->cl_mod_rpcs_in_flight++;
at next it will be
max = max(cli->cl_max_mod_rpcs_in_flight, cli->cl_mod_rpcs_in_flight);
lprocfs_oh_tally(&cli->cl_mod_rpcs_hist,
cli->cl_mod_rpcs_in_flight);
/* find a free tag */
i = find_first_zero_bit(cli->cl_mod_tag_bitmap,
max + 1);
(tag bitmap size isn't checked) so we easy to have a bit outside of
LASSERT(i < OBD_MAX_RIF_MAX);

OOPS, panic.

Oh, I thought you were meaning that there is some upper limit on slot numbers that is checked on the MDS, which would need protocol changes or tuning to fix. This looks like a limit that is totally internal to the client, and a matter of a few bytes in the bitmap.

It is pretty unlikely that there will suddenly be 1000 extra RPCs in flight for a single MDT, but that static limit could be checked for the extreme case, rather than reverting the fix. Conversely, allowing 999 extra inodes to be freed under memory pressure can be very useful and will allow forward progress.

I think we can have much better fix. we needs to avoid a cancel any open locks in the memory pleasure case, like it does for replay import -> cancel used.
please don't forget close rpc are SYNC. so memory pleasure blocked until close will processed. I don't think this is good.

Some things I see when looking at this code in more detail:

  • there is no way to return any kind of error from ll_delete_inode() or ll_clear_inode() so no way to stop this inode cleanup
  • there doesn't appear to be any way to push the cleanup to another thread since the caller is expecting to reap the inode upon return
  • trying to allocate a larger bitmap in this code path seems counter-productive
  • it is very strange that memory shrinking is calling into the filesystem code and not allowed to block?
  • are we missing some kind of GFP flag or similar that prevents these inodes from being cleaned up?
  • there is unfortunately no kernel version information in this bug report to know if this was some kind of kernel bug

That said, until we have some better patch, I'm not in favor of doing more than change the console message into CDEBUG(D_RPCTRACE), since an oops "now" is still worse than an oops after cleaning up 512 more inodes.

>there is no way to return any kind of error from ll_delete_inode() or ll_clear_inode() so no way to stop this inode cleanup
simples way to avoid to be place in the LRU for inodes with open lock. other ways in the inode_lru_isolate.

        /*
         * Inodes can get referenced, redirtied, or repopulated while
         * they're already on the LRU, and this can make them
         * unreclaimable for a while. Remove them lazily here; iput,
         * sync, or the last page cache deletion will requeue them.
         */
        if (atomic_read(&inode->i_count) ||
            (inode->i_state & ~I_REFERENCED) ||
            !mapping_shrinkable(&inode->i_data)) {
                list_lru_isolate(lru, &inode->i_lru);
                spin_unlock(&inode->i_lock);
                this_cpu_dec(nr_unused);
                return LRU_REMOVED;
        }

>there doesn't appear to be any way to push the cleanup to another thread since the caller is expecting to reap the inode upon return
this is possible but it's too hard. Close RPC might to be async in this particular case, but it needs a slot handing to be done in ptlrpcd code, which not a trivial. I started to do it, but it not easy.
A specially ptlrpc_queue_wait needs to be converted into ptlrpd code. This is done. But have no time for next step for now.

>trying to allocate a larger bitmap in this code path seems counter-productive
no way. server should to have same bitmap size, both sides limited with OBD_MAX_RIF_MAX.

>it is very strange that memory shrinking is calling into the filesystem code and not allowed to block?

        if (inode_has_buffers(inode) || !mapping_empty(&inode->i_data)) {
                inode_pin_lru_isolating(inode);
                spin_unlock(&inode->i_lock);
                spin_unlock(&lru->lock);
                if (remove_inode_buffers(inode)) {
                        unsigned long reap;
                        reap = invalidate_mapping_pages(&inode->i_data, 0, -1);
                        if (current_is_kswapd())
                                __count_vm_events(KSWAPD_INODESTEAL, reap);
                        else
                                __count_vm_events(PGINODESTEAL, reap);
                        mm_account_reclaimed_pages(reap);
                }
                inode_unpin_lru_isolating(inode);
                return LRU_RETRY;
        }

btw, it's allow to block - but lustre network might to be very very slow. I don't think someone expect a block for ~AT_MAX (aka 450s).
